title: Bicarbonate–albumin coupling does not establish incremental cross-cycle handgrip prediction
abstract: A literature-motivated, registered test asked whether a serum bicarbonate-by-albumin interaction improves combined handgrip prediction beyond flexible additive conventional measures. Weighted ridge models trained in 2,040 NHANES 2011–2012 adults aged 50+ were frozen and evaluated in 2,267 separately sampled 2013–2014 adults. The interaction changed weighted MSE from 120.1762 to 120.2161 kg²; baseline-minus-augmented gain was −0.0399 (joint source–target stratified PSU bootstrap 95% interval −1.2694 to 0.4125). Source grouped cross-validation also worsened. There is no demonstrated incremental predictive benefit for this representation; this is not equivalence or evidence against physiological acid–base effects on muscle. Transfer is temporal within one survey system, with complete-case and shared-protocol limitations.

citations.reason: Primary handgrip and lower-extremity evidence motivating a cautious test
